name: Building Revision Into Class
title: Building Revision Into Class
answer: Building revision into class means making drafting, AI feedback, student revision, peer discussion, and teacher-guided class reflection a regular part of the lesson. It matters because students need a reason to engage with feedback, and the teacher moves from writing every comment to guiding the process. Teachers also review AI feedback before students see it, at least until they know how a tool behaves.

sections.body: The idea is to treat revision as part of the lesson rather than an optional afterthought. A proposed model has students draft, receive AI feedback, revise on their own, discuss revisions with peers, and then reflect as a class with the teacher guiding. Each step gives students a reason to engage with the feedback. This solves the problem of feedback that students may not act on, and it changes the teacher's role from writing every comment to guiding the process. Goal setting is added so students have a clear reason to revise.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, a teacher builds a short goal setting step into every revision cycle. A student might set a specific goal, such as adding evidence to each paragraph, which gives a clear reason to revise. The text gives one grade band example: in a study with 345 upper secondary students learning English, goal setting based on automated scores produced the largest gains in revision. For those older students, the cycle can include drafting, AI feedback, independent revision, peer discussion, and class reflection with the teacher guiding. Teachers should review AI feedback before students see it, at least until they know how a tool behaves.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text does not give a formal evidence label, but it cites research for this idea. Helm and Hesse (2026) proposed a model in which students draft, receive AI feedback, revise on their own, discuss their revisions with peers, and then reflect as a class with the teacher guiding. In a study with 345 upper secondary students learning English, goal setting based on automated scores produced the largest gains in revision (Jansen et al., 2024). The text also notes that Chapter 13 described how AI feedback can misread English learners' writing.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits and risks are clear in the text. Teachers should review AI feedback before students see it, at least until they know how a tool behaves. A quick scan can catch errors, harsh wording, or feedback that misses the point. Feedback released without review can confuse or discourage students, and the text notes that AI feedback can misread English learners' writing. The decisions that stay with a person are reviewing the feedback, guiding the revision process, and building the goal setting step into the cycle.
